KEY INSIGHTS

Substantial marketplace scale, with clear growth-quality risks to address.

The marketplace has meaningful breadth, but the operating story is not simply “growth.” Seller value is concentrated, seller activation is slow, and delivery performance is strongly associated with customer-experience risk.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Marketplace scale is meaningful, but growth quality depends on what happens after seller acquisition.

This opening page is written for management: it separates marketplace scale from growth quality, identifies the three risks that deserve attention, and defines the measurement boundary before any action is recommended.

KEY FINDINGS

Breadth improved in the last complete month, but value depth weakened.

From Jul→Aug 2018, orders increased 2.9% and active sellers 1.3%, while GMV fell 4.6%, AOV fell 7.2%, and GMV per active seller fell 5.8%.

BUSINESS INTERPRETATION

More activity does not automatically mean healthier growth.

Marketplace breadth and seller productivity are moving differently. Management should avoid using order count or seller count as a standalone health signal.

RECOMMENDED ACTION

Manage growth quality, not just top-line volume.

Track volume, value per transaction, seller productivity, activation speed and customer experience as one operating system.

DETAILED ANALYSIS

Marketplace performance: growth breadth versus value depth

The data indicates that the marketplace is not simply “growing” or “declining”. The final complete-month comparison shows two different stories happening at the same time. Transaction breadth improved: orders increased 2.9% and active sellers increased 1.3%. But value depth weakened: GMV fell 4.6%, AOV fell 7.2%, and GMV per active seller fell 5.8%. This means more activity is flowing through the marketplace, but each transaction and each active seller is generating less value than in the prior complete month.

From a management perspective, that changes the question from “Are we growing?” to “What type of growth are we creating?” If the team only watches order count, the picture looks positive. If it only watches GMV, the picture looks negative. The correct interpretation is that breadth expanded while monetization/productivity softened. That is exactly why executive reporting should separate volume, AOV, seller productivity and customer-experience health rather than compressing everything into one headline KPI.

Measurement integrity is the second critical point. A naïve payment × order-item join inflates GMV by 4.54%, roughly R$617.5K. At executive level, that is not a minor technical detail; it is large enough to change how performance is interpreted. The project therefore treats grain-safe metric construction as part of the business decision process, not as back-office data cleaning.

Management implication

Use this page as the weekly health check: first confirm the reporting period is valid, then read volume, value and productivity together. If orders rise while AOV and GMV/seller fall again, the next diagnostic should move into category mix, seller mix and acquisition/activation quality rather than celebrating volume growth.

EXECUTIVE IMPLICATION

The first management decision is to trust the metric before reacting to the trend.

Raw order observations continue beyond Aug 2018, but executive-complete reporting ends on 31 Aug 2018. Partial Sep/Oct tail periods are excluded from performance conclusions so that a source-cutoff problem is not mistaken for a commercial collapse.

ANALYTICAL BOUNDARY

Historical decision-support case study, not a current-market forecast.

GMV is a proxy rather than platform revenue or profit. Marketing cost is unavailable, so CAC and ROAS are not estimated. Channel, onboarding, and delivery findings are observational and are not presented as causal effects.

Release rule: claims shown on the site follow the governed analytical outputs in the repository; incomplete periods and non-observable cohorts are excluded or explicitly flagged.
